prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you ate a salad at a barbecue. Respond to the committee.
response:
Mr. Chairman, members of the Committee:

I categorically deny the implication that my conduct at the barbecue was un-American. Yes, I was seen in proximity to a salad. Yes, I may have placed a modest portion of coleslaw on a paper plate. But let the record show that this was done alongside ribs, burgers, hot dogs, and an amount of potato chips consistent with patriotic norms.

Furthermore, I refuse to accept the false choice between grilled meats and side dishes. A cookout is a broad coalition. Beans, corn, watermelon, macaroni salad, and even leafy greens have all, at times, stood beside the barbecue pit in service of the common good.

If loving a balanced plate is wrong, then I ask this Committee: who among us has not taken a scoop of “just to try it” pasta salad because someone’s aunt was watching?

I have never been, nor am I now, a member of any anti-barbecue organization. I remain loyal to charcoal, propane, smoke, sauce, and the inalienable right of every American to go back for seconds.

Thank you.
